study.title: Acupuncture Modulates the Functional Connectivity of the Default Mode Network in Stroke Patients
study.study_design: Within-subject pre-post resting-state fMRI study with healthy controls as a comparison group; nonrepeated event-related-fMRI (NRER-fMRI) design
study.population: Eight right hemispheric infarction and stable ischemic stroke patients and ten healthy subjects
study.disease_condition: Right hemispheric ischemic stroke (corona radiate, internal capsule, or basal ganglia infarction)
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) first episode of stroke; (2) being between 35 and 80 years old; (3) being right-handed; (4) 2–12 weeks after the onset of stroke; (5) sufficient cognition to follow simple commands, MMSE (Mini-Mental State Examination score) > 21
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) bilateral infarcts; (2) recurrent stroke; (3) any previous history of alcohol or drug abuse; (4) history of epilepsy or other neurological diseases and psychiatric disorders; (5) serious cognitive deficits; (6) being with any MRI contraindications

extraction_notes.note: The paper reports that coordinates are 'mapped in Talairach space' (Table 2 and Table 3 footnotes, Section 2.5), but the ROI for the PCC is defined in MNI coordinates (0, −56, 25) in Section 2.4. The functional images were normalized to MNI space. It is unclear whether final coordinate results in the tables are true Talairach coordinates or MNI coordinates labeled as Talairach. No conversion method is described.
No sham acupuncture condition was included in this study. The study compares stroke patients with healthy controls under the same verum acupuncture. There is no sham/placebo arm.
Expectancy, credibility, blinding success, and allocation guessing measures were not assessed or reported in this study.

Full deqi questionnaire data (subscale scores, group comparisons) are reported in a separate paper: Bai et al. (2013) 'Acupuncture De Qi in stable somatosensory stroke patients: relations with effective brain network for motor recovery,' reference [28]. Only the absence of sharp pain is reported here.

The statistical analysis used both two-sample t-tests and paired t-tests (stated in Section 2.5), but it is not explicitly clear from each table which test was applied for each specific contrast. Table 2 footnote states 'two-sample t-test (df = 16)' and Table 3 footnote also states 'two-sample t-test (df = 16)'. However, the within-group pre-post comparisons (post-acupuncture vs baseline) would logically require paired t-tests. The df = 16 is consistent with a two-sample t-test on 18 subjects. This is flagged as a potential inconsistency.

In Table 3, the cluster size threshold stated in the footnote is '>76 voxels' (consistent with Table 2), yet the reported cluster sizes for stroke patients' increased connectivity are 21 and 28 voxels, which are below this threshold. This inconsistency is present in the paper as published and may reflect a different threshold applied to the within-group analysis or an error in the footnote.

Table 3 footnote states 'two-sample t-test (df = 16)' for all results, but the within-group pre/post comparisons (increased/decreased connectivity to the PCC in control subjects and stroke patients) would typically use paired t-tests. The paper mentions both two-sample t-test and paired t-test in Section 2.5 but does not clearly assign each to a specific contrast.
No session-level clinical outcome data (e.g., changes in NIHSS or MMSE post-acupuncture) are reported. Clinical scores are reported only at baseline in Table 1.

The table heading for Table 3 states 'Results of the control subjects and stroke patients after acupuncture procedures.' The within-group post vs. baseline comparisons and between-group comparisons are combined in this single table without clear separation, which could cause ambiguity in interpreting which comparison is which.
The paper does not report a PMID. The DOI is provided as 10.1155/2014/765413.

Healthy controls underwent the same NRER-fMRI acupuncture paradigm but the intervention entry for healthy controls during stimulation is inferred from the methods section, which does not explicitly state differences between stroke and healthy control procedures.
